summary.text: Andrew Cheeseman is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Frankston at the 2026 Victorian election. He says he has spent most of his life in the Frankston area and works in video production and editing; earlier he audited airline records. He ran for the party at the 2024 Frankston City Council election.

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC describes him as a Victorian Socialists candidate at this council election but does not give the result or the ward.

priorities.text: I stand for taxing landlords until they scream, then taxing them some more.
Bringing privatised public services back into public hands, paid for by higher taxes on the wealthy
Ending what he calls subsidies for property investors while public housing is sold
Pledges to keep no more than a median wage if elected and give the rest to community campaigns

sources.title: Frankston: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Andrew Cheeseman, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Bree Ambry is the Liberal candidate for Frankston at the 2026 Victorian election. A former nurse, she now manages healthcare operations at the Royal Flying Doctor Service. In the community she is the Frankston Dolphins Netball Club's secretary and a lifesaving trainer with the Frankston Life Saving Club.

occupation.text: Healthcare operations manager, Royal Flying Doctor Service

priorities.text: Fixing potholes, opening hospital beds that sit unused and upgrading local sports clubs
The Liberal platform of cutting crime and living costs and making government work better

summary.text: Chrysten Abraham is standing as an independent in Frankston at the 2026 Victorian election. She works in human resources, a career she began in disability and home care, and holds a business degree from RMIT. She has run three times before: for the Liberal Democrats in Flinders (2022 federal) and Frankston (2022 state), and for the Libertarians at the 2024 Dunkley by-election.

summary.text: Henry Kelsall is standing as an independent for Frankston at the 2026 Victorian election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Someone of the same name has stood at Frankston-area elections since the late 1990s: for the Greens in Frankston in 1999 and 2002, in Carrum in 2010 and 2014 and in the federal seat of Dunkley in 1998 and 2001, and as an independent in Frankston in 2018 and 2022, when he won 0.9% of the primary vote. No source links those campaigns to the 2026 candidate, and neither the ABC nor a campaign page had published a biography as at 9 Nov 2026.

summary.text: Dr Julie Harman is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Frankston at the 2026 Victorian election. A registered nurse before she studied medicine, she worked in Melbourne hospitals, in Indigenous health on Thursday Island and overseas as a Médecins Sans Frontières volunteer, and graduated as a doctor in 2016. For about six years she has worked as a doctor with the Australian Defence Force's recruitment team.

prior_roles.role: Hospital doctor (Box Hill, Maroondah and Angliss hospitals)
Registered nurse (Alfred, Box Hill and Monash hospitals)
Indigenous health care worker, Thursday Island

priorities.text: An end to factory farming, with investment in plant-based proteins
Protecting parks and open space from overdevelopment
Tougher laws on recycling and pollution
More funding for education, mental health and public housing
More training jobs, small business growth and tourism in Frankston

summary.text: Katie Goulas is the Greens candidate for Frankston at the 2026 Victorian election. She works in retail, is studying for a master's degree in justice and criminology, and volunteers as an advocate for children held in youth detention. She says she is standing on housing, health, community safety and climate.

occupation.text: Retail worker; postgraduate student in justice and criminology

prior_roles.role: Volunteer advocate for children in youth detention

priorities.text: Affordable housing
Better health services
Safer communities
Strong action on climate change and sustainable living

He became a minister in 2026 and is now responsible for police, crime prevention, emergency services and multicultural affairs. He is recontesting Frankston in 2026.

summary.text: Peter Nicholes is the Family First candidate for Frankston at the 2026 Victorian election. A full-time pastor who has lived in Frankston for more than 37 years, he earlier worked as a physical education teacher and gym manager, and is on the leadership team of the Crosslink Christian Network. He ran for Family First in Dunkley at the 2025 federal election.

prior_roles.role: Physical education teacher and gym manager

priorities.text: Protecting free speech, especially for parents
The family as the basis of society, and parents' right to raise children without undue state interference
Giving young people identity and purpose as a way to reduce youth crime
Bringing Australia's many cultures together as one nation
